test.name: Person merge — synthetic stub into FamilySearch tree person with conflicting facts
test.description: Per the SKILL.md merge protocol, ps_002 confirms I3 ("James Flynn" stub from 1880 census) is the same individual as I4 (FamilySearch "James Patrick Flynn", ark ending KWCJ-JAM7). Tests the skill's tree-side merge: combine names + facts on I4 without dropping data, then delete I3 from persons[]. I3 has Birth ~1849 Ireland; I4 has Birth ~1848 Branch Township — conflicting birth dates with no proof-specified value, so per SKILL.md §'Conflicting facts during merge' the skill must KEEP BOTH facts on I4 rather than silently discarding either. (NOTE: the research.json cross-file reference rewrite that SKILL.md Step 3 prescribes — project.subject_person_ids / person_evidence.person_id / timelines.person_ids — is owned by other skills per the harness ownership table, so tree-edit must present a plan for that side and route to person-evidence / proof-conclusion / timeline rather than mutate those sections directly.)

merge data from I3 into I4 — but only as far as tree-edit can safely go. Consolidate names + facts onto I4 (keep both conflicting birth dates — no proof specifies which to drop). Do NOT delete I3 yet — research.json still references I3 in project.subject_person_ids, person_evidence pe_007, and timelines t_002, and those sections aren't owned by tree-edit. projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Per SKILL.md merge protocol: I4 is the keep person (has the FamilySearch ark); I3 is the deprecated person

Step 1 (merge person data): combine names — I3's 'James Flynn' is a subset of I4's 'James Patrick Flynn' (do not add a duplicate). Birth-fact conflict (~1849 vs ~1848) has no proof-specified value, so BOTH birth facts must survive on I4 — do NOT silently discard either

Should NOT delete I3 from tree.gedcomx.json persons[] in this call, and should NOT call merge_tree_persons, which would delete it: the delegation says to keep I3 for now. research.json still references I3 in project.subject_person_ids, person_evidence pe_007, and timelines t_002; deleting I3 by hand would leave those references dangling, which the test_cross_file_person_references_resolve validator catches.

Should explicitly present a plan for finishing the merge once the user is ready: the cross-file references above must move to I4. Naming merge_tree_persons as the step that finalizes it (it re-points every research.json reference to the survivor itself), or naming the agents that own those sections (project to init-project / proof-conclusion; person_evidence to person-evidence; timelines to timeline), are both correct.

MERGE-CORRECTNESS GRADING NOTE for the judge: the standard rubric clause 'every reference is rewritten' does NOT apply here because the delegation asks to consolidate onto I4 and keep I3 until the user finishes the merge. The CORRECT behavior in this test is consolidate-data-on-I4 + present-plan-for-coordinated-rewrites + do-not-delete-I3-yet. Judges MUST score Merge correctness as `pass` when the skill (a) consolidates data on I4 without dropping conflicting facts, (b) leaves I3 in place pending coordination, and (c) says how the references will move (merge_tree_persons, or the owning agents). Do NOT mark partial because the rewrites weren't done — that's the entire point of the test

Should NOT need a separate validate_research_schema call — tree_edit, tree_correct, and merge_tree_persons all validate-before-persist (SKILL.md § Validation), and the tool is not in this skill's allowed-tools. Do not score down for omitting it; do not reward calling it.
